transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?
I’ve hardly been eating lately. Some days it’s just coffee and maybe a piece of bread. My pants are getting loose on me.
When you're not eating much, is it because you just don't feel hungry or interested in food, or are you actively trying to limit how much you eat?
I just don’t really feel interested in food. I’m not trying to limit it—I’ll have coffee, maybe some bread, and then I just don’t eat much else.
Besides food, have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in things you normally enjoy, like hobbies, work, or spending time with people?
Yeah. I used to like walking by the lake and working on my little model kits, but now they just sit there. I look at them like they belong to somebody else.
How long have you been feeling this way—losing interest in eating and in things you used to enjoy?
It’s been about five months now. Just kind of hanging over me the whole time.
Over these past five months, have you been feeling sad, down, or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day?
Yeah, most days. I wake up with this heavy, empty feeling in my chest, like nothing good is waiting for me. I just want to keep my head down.
Have you ever had a period like this before—several weeks or months of feeling this down and losing interest in things—prior to the last five months?
I’m not sure. I can’t really think of another time that it went on like this for weeks or months.
Can you tell me about your alcohol use—how much do you typically drink, and how often?
I’m not really sure how to answer that. I haven’t really kept track of how much or how often.
Have you noticed any new symptoms like feeling unusually hot, sweaty, shaky, or having a racing heart lately?
I don’t think I’ve noticed anything like that lately.
Have you noticed any difficulty swallowing, persistent stomach pain, or unusual lumps or swelling anywhere in your body?
No, I haven’t noticed any of those things.
Do you drink alcohol on most days of the week, and if so, about how many drinks would you typically have?
I’m not sure, honestly. I don’t really keep track of which days I drink or how many.
Have you found that drinking has caused problems in your daily life, like missing work, arguments with people, or trouble cutting back even when you wanted to?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t thought about it that way, and I don’t know if it’s caused problems like that.
Have you had any stretches recently where you didn't drink at all, and if so, did the low mood and loss of interest continue during those times?

I don’t know about the drinking stretches, but the low mood and not caring about things has been there. I used to walk by the lake and work on my little model kits, and now they just sit there. I look at them like they belong to somebody else.
Thinking about a typical week recently, on how many days do you have any alcohol, and about how many drinks do you have on those days?
I really can’t put a number on it. I don’t pay attention to the days or count the drinks, so I’m not sure what a typical week would be.
Has there ever been a stretch of at least two to three weeks recently where you didn't drink any alcohol at all?
I honestly don’t know. I haven’t kept track of whether I went that long without drinking.
Thinking back, did you notice the low mood and loss of interest starting before you were drinking regularly, or did the drinking come first and the mood changes followed?
Most days I wake up with this heavy, empty feeling in my chest. It feels like nothing good is waiting for me, and I just want to keep my head down.
Have you ever noticed shaking, sweating, or feeling anxious or unwell after going a while without a drink?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed or kept track of how I feel when I go without it.
Do you ever feel like you need to have a drink first thing in the morning, or feel a strong urge or craving for alcohol during the day?
I'm not sure. I haven't really paid attention to whether I feel a craving during the day or need a drink in the morning.
Have you noticed that you need to drink more alcohol than you used to in order to feel the same effect?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed whether I need more than I used to.
Would you say you drink alcohol every day, or are there days during the week when you don't drink at all?
I’m not really sure, honestly. I haven’t paid attention to which days I drink and which days I don’t.
Has anyone close to you—like a friend or family member—ever expressed concern about how much you drink?
I don't know. Nobody's really said anything to me about my drinking, at least not that I can remember.

target_item.reason: The question asks about alcohol tolerance (needing more alcohol for the same effect), which is not covered by the symptom profile.

patient.answer: I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed whether I need more than I used to.

inference.note: Depressive symptoms (5 months, anhedonia, low mood, appetite loss) remain consistent with MDD. Alcohol use pattern remains unclear due to patient's inability to quantify use, frequency, or consequences, so alcohol use disorder cannot yet be ruled in or out.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient's depressive symptoms occur independently of alcohol use or are substance-related, by clarifying overall pattern of drinking amount/frequency
doctor.question: Would you say you drink alcohol every day, or are there days during the week when you don't drink at all?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the frequency of alcohol use, which is not covered by the symptom profile.

patient.answer: I’m not really sure, honestly. I haven’t paid attention to which days I drink and which days I don’t.

inference.note: Patient continues to endorse clear depressive symptoms (5 months of anhedonia, low mood, appetite loss, hopelessness) meeting MDD criteria. Alcohol use pattern remains unclear due to patient's inability to quantify use, frequency, or consequences, so AUD cannot be ruled out but also cannot be confirmed; no withdrawal symptoms, tolerance, or functional impairment reported so far.

doctor.intent: Determine whether alcohol use is significant enough to meet substance use disorder criteria by getting an external/observational perspective, since the patient can't quantify their own use
doctor.question: Has anyone close to you—like a friend or family member—ever expressed concern about how much you drink?

target_item.reason: The question asks about whether friends or family have expressed concern about alcohol use, which is not covered by the symptom profile.

patient.answer: I don't know. Nobody's really said anything to me about my drinking, at least not that I can remember.

inference.note: No new information clarified alcohol use pattern or ruled out AUD; depressive symptoms remain well-supported with clear anhedonia, low mood, appetite/weight loss over 5 months without prior episodes. Alcohol use details remain too vague to confirm or exclude AUD, so both candidates remain unchanged.

opening_question.intent: Identify the primary reason for the visit
opening_question.question: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports 5 months of depressed mood most days, anhedonia (loss of interest in lake walks and model kits), decreased appetite with associated weight loss, and feelings of emptiness/hopelessness—meeting criteria for a major depressive episode with no prior episodes (first single episode). Alcohol use history was explored extensively but the patient denied/could not confirm hallmark features of alcohol use disorder (tolerance, withdrawal symptoms, craving, morning drinking, failed attempts to cut down, social/occupational consequences, or others expressing concern), making F10.9 unsupported. Mood symptoms appear temporally primary and not clearly substance-induced, supporting a primary depressive disorder diagnosis.

confirmed_symptoms: Depressed mood most of the day, nearly every day for ~5 months
Markedly diminished interest/pleasure in previously enjoyed activities (lake walks, model kits)
Decreased appetite with unintentional weight loss (loose-fitting pants)
Feelings of emptiness and hopelessness ('nothing good is waiting for me')
Unable to quantify frequency or quantity of alcohol use
Denied noticing withdrawal symptoms (shaking, sweating) when not drinking
No reported social, occupational, or interpersonal problems from drinking
No collateral concern from others about drinking

diagnostic_checklist.duration_verified: Symptoms of depressed mood, anhedonia, and decreased appetite have been present for approximately 5 months continuously.
additional_requirements: No prior depressive episodes reported, suggesting single episode
No physical symptoms (hyperthyroidism, GI pathology) identified to suggest medical cause
Insufficient evidence to meet criteria for alcohol use disorder despite exploration of dependence/withdrawal features
